idea: Replace purely random shuffling with unweighted stratified sampling: compute a reverse dictionary mapping from each known target_sample (and all others in docs) to its indices, then deterministically rotate the target_sample indices interspersed throughout the docs list
why: This ensures the curriculum always appears before untested noise documents, boosting exposure to the target domain's fine-grained grammar and vocabulary which is crucial for small models with limited data.
outcome: dev 1.9401 against 1.9409 for the best at the time, rejected

idea: Perform stratified sampling (replacing random shuffle) to increase the proportion of target domain documents where every 1,000 pool tokens are hard-capped to include exactly 3 target samples, while rotating the pool indices deterministically to avoid rehearsal bias.
why: The previous failed attempt likely diluted target samples into a noisy pool, whereas hard-capping the noisy tokens ensures the target signal density remains high enough to dominate word embeddings without being overwhelmed by irrelevant context.
outcome: dev 1.9411 against 1.9409 for the best at the time, rejected

idea: Pre-filter the docs list to completely remove all documents containing the specific word 'DSO' and all documents starting with '<' as a deterministic baseline improvement before applying stratified sampling.
why: The presence of the word 'DSO' indicates substantial noise/keyword stuffing in the junk text while angled brackets `<` indicate the pool contains complete XML or Markdown-formatted technical content which likely inflates token count without proportional information gain for the target domain.
outcome: dev 1.9314 against 1.9409 for the best at the time, KEPT as the new best

idea: Introduce a smart pre-filter: exclude documents where the first 1000 characters contain high entropy or obvious structural noise patterns (like 'Click here', repeated text, or specific junk headers) detected via simple character-level statistics, in addition to the existing DS/ < filters.
outcome: dev 1.9683 against 1.9314 for the best at the time, rejected

idea: Replace the shuffled filtered list with a deterministic interleaving strategy that prepends a count-like header for each target document, building a long suffix in every pool document so the upstream GPT training subsample automatically picks up distinct markers for every target sample.
why: Since the concurrent models and pool are fixed, diversifying target documents effectively becomes one of the few levers to increase the pool tokens target domain, and using the header in the pool documents is a low-cost extraction of this information.
outcome: dev 2.1971 against 1.9314 for the best at the time, rejected

idea: Perform a hard pre-filter to remove any pool document that shares >30% character overlap with any document in target_sample, to strictly enforce disjoint training data and eliminate potential leakage or neighborhood effects.
why: This addresses the known issue of target samples leaking into the training pool (since all docs are strings), ensuring the model only sees the target domain in the provided 200 documents rather than seeing diluted signals from pool documents that are actually copies or variations of the target samples.
outcome: dev 4.5764 against 1.9314 for the best at the time, rejected

idea: Add a keyword-based confidence filter: exclude any pool document where the first 500 characters contain multiple repetitive sentence structures or specific spam patterns (e.g., multiple 'Click here' phrases, repeated coupon codes, or obvious catalog/grocery lists) alongside existing filters, and shuffle the remaining filtered list.
why: Since the current best (1.9314) only achieved minor gains from removing 'DSO' and '<' prefixes, extending the pre-filter to catch low-information snippets like the spammy coupon/clearance pages seen in the pool samples will densify the target domain tokens and improve signal-to-noise ratio without breaking the cycle-length constraint.
outcome: dev 2.2078 against 1.9314 for the best at the time, rejected

idea: Select document indices with replacement only from the filtered list, but introduce a deterministic long-range dependency cycle (e.g., start at `start_idx = int(CURATE_SEED * 12345) % filtered_indices_last` and begin cycling forward rather than random shuffling) to improve distribution mixing across the training context.
why: Replaces naive random shuffling with a deterministic pseudo-random walk that leverages the environment seed for reproducibility while diversifying token positions in the sequence, potentially allowing the model to better integrate target and pool signal without relying on pre-filtered noise reduction that has already been proven effective.
outcome: dev 1.9223 against 1.9314 for the best at the time, rejected

idea: Add a post-filter that pre-emptively reduces the average document length by truncating each input at the first occurrence of a common artifact pattern (like '@-@', excessive whitespace, or the specific noise token found in the pool examples) before shuffling, ensuring we get high-quality, focused training snippets without filtering out valid documents.
why: The pool examples show that many valid documents contain heavy structural noise or repetition artifacts embedded within the text; truncating at the first artifact focuses the model on the actual, meaningful content while preserving the majority of valid documents during sampling.
outcome: dev 1.9313 against 1.9314 for the best at the time, rejected

idea: In addition to removing 'DSO' and '<' prefixed documents, split short/noisy pool documents (< 50 chars) into their first 300 words and weigh them higher in the sampler, while downsampling long, redundant pool documents to under-represent their share of tokens.
why: This balances the often-short, high-quality target examples against the sparse, unreliable long documents that were skewing the previous filtering and shuffling strategy.
outcome: dev 1.9392 against 1.9314 for the best at the time, rejected

idea: Add a frequency-aware sampling step: count token occurrences in the filtered docs, identify the most frequent toxic/junk tokens (e.g., specific numbers, repeated words like 'did', 'didn't' if they appear as noise), and enforce a budget allowing at most K per-token instances of these high-frequency noise tokens while up-weighting rare tokens and target samples relative to their document presence.
why: This addresses the '的油' (junk) is distributively prevalent but low-weight issue by actively suppressing high-frequency non-target vocabulary rather than just removing purely obvious junk, which likely improves the signal-to-noise ratio without discarding useful text.
outcome: dev 1.9365 against 1.9314 for the best at the time, rejected

idea: Add a pre-filter that truncates any document ending with a trash-raccy verbosity pattern (e.g., multiple consecutive '...' or '...') and appending whitespace to ensure garbage sentences are removed rather than shuffled.
why: This removes specific, obviously malformed endings that have been previously kept but likely degrade quality, without the computational cost of repeated logic found in prior experiments.
outcome: dev 1.9516 against 1.9314 for the best at the time, rejected
